findings.title: Explicit midnight timestamps become whole-day bounds
findings.description: Pydantic parses `"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"` as a `date` with this date-first union. Consequently, `resolve_window()` expands an explicit midnight `end` to `23:59:59.999999`, returning almost an extra day. Reproduced using the actual window resolver. Both endpoints are affected. Preserve the distinction between date-only and datetime inputs, and add midnight-bound regression tests.

findings.title: Response construction blocks the event loop
findings.description: Only database reads run in the executor; model construction and serialization execute synchronously inside the async handler. An isolated benchmark of the actual candle models at 75,000 rows measured approximately **803 ms** for construction and **350 ms** for `model_dump()` alone—far beyond the required 1 ms bound. Other requests cannot progress on that event loop during this work. Move construction and encoding off-loop after releasing the connection. Apply the same fix to trades and test event-loop responsiveness under large concurrent responses.

findings.title: Concurrent inserts can bypass the row ceiling
findings.description: Count and fetch are separate statements without a repeatable-read snapshot. The inspected pool configuration does not establish stronger isolation, so concurrent collection commits can increase the fetched result after admission. `_admit_rows()` checks only the earlier count; neither fetch has a limit or subsequent size check. Both endpoints can therefore return more than the configured ceiling, potentially by an entire inserted batch. Use a consistent snapshot for count/fetch and add a concurrent-insert regression test.
